facts.text: Palmyra was named after the ancient Syrian city, a suggestion from Taggart's daughter Jeanette, who drew inspiration from their former hometown in New York.
Taggart, an architect and stone cutter, dedicated a four‑block village park in his honor, now known as Taggart Park.
The Midland Pacific Railway arrived in 1871, laying tracks parallel to the old trail and sparking rapid settlement in Palmyra.
Every early June, Palmyra hosts the Old Settlers Picnic—a weekend of family games, a parade, pedal tractor pull, cornhole, and a color run.
Preservation efforts include the 1984 Senior Citizens' Activities Center, Taggart Park restorations, and the Pioneer Cemetery’s 2021 National Register listing.
